    AI Overview
    The U.S. stock market (NYSE and Nasdaq) is closed on Friday, April 3, 2026, in observance of
    Good Friday. 
    Here are the key details: 
    • Reason for Closure: Good Friday is a recognized holiday for the stock exchanges, a tradition dating back to the late 19th century.
    • Bond Market: The U.S. bond market is not closed completely, but it is holding an abbreviated session, closing at noon ET.
    • Not a Federal Holiday: Although the stock market is closed, Good Friday is not a federal holiday, meaning banks and other services may still be open.
    • When Markets Reopen: Regular trading hours for the NYSE and Nasdaq will resume on Monday, April 6, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. ET.
    • Next Holiday: The next scheduled market closure is on Monday, May 25, 2026, for Memorial Day.
